item.title: -1, alas
item.content:encoded:
Like said a wise man :

The second big thing to consider when making a humanoid SCP object is avoiding "X-men Syndrome". As a rule of thumb, if what's anomalous about your humanoid SCP object can be most accurately described as a voluntary "power" or "ability", you should probably start over. Slapping on some superficially nasty drawbacks, making them ugly, and/or giving them an awful personality won't fix it, either.

The story is not bad per se (even if quite light, mostly a twist with text added around it), but SCP-638 is just not a decent SCP.

item.title: Re: Really, Really Quicksand
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open
[-] Close

Here's some crit:

An outdated article consisting of ConProcs, Description, Exploration Logs. A second article locked to higher-clearance staff consisting of ConProcs, Description, and Addendum."

Is this extremely necessary? I assume you want to include the fact that new holes are created by the anomaly in the "updated" one, but does that add anything? I feel like it would break the flow of things, you could just say "prior to XX/XX/XX this property was unknown" or whatever, I think that would be a better option.

sending test subjects down the "invisible hole" to their deaths in futile attempts to find out where it leads.

If the subjects are being lowered into the hole, what happens? Do they just lose video/recording contact and the rope goes slack or what? And if the first two D-Class sent in go missing, why doesn't the Foundation just send in some mole-rats or another MTF?

The Foundation builds a site around this area and begins to study it

Why does this hole warrant a whole site to be built around it, surely they can just throw a tarp over it and say "keep out"?

Central Narrative:

This paragraph is what concerns me the most, there's no narrative here. This is simply "the Foundation does some stuff to the hole and some other stuff happens and then they contain it even though it's barely a threat in the first place."

item.title: SCP Idea Whale Eating Bird
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: No, at least not yet.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre:I haven't settled on one yet, though it will likely be action/suspense.

Layout: Information presentation

Elevator Pitch: A Keter class giant bird, living on an island in the Pacific, hunting whales like an osprey. Unnaturally large and fast, it occasionally attacks human ships.

Central Narrative: The Foundation deploys operatives to the North Pacific after a large bird attacks a group of whale watchers. After some investigation, they are unable to find anything, but stay posted. A few years later, a surfaced Soviet Submarine is sunk by the creature. The Foundation ramps up the search, eventually tracking it to a remote island between Chile and New Zealand. A submarine is sent to drop off a scout crew, but the sub is sunk because they underestimate how deep the creature can dive. A cruiser is deployed, and fires upon the creature when it attempts to dive at it. The bird survives, but the mission is called off to avoid potentially killing it. Another sub is deployed, this time equipped with an improved diving system to get down faster, and more ships surrounding the area to track it by RADAR. The crew treks up the small dormant volcanic island, and finds a nest made of logs with scattered bones. When the RADAR team radios them to say that the bird is returning home, they quickly find that it is coming faster than expected, and the submarine that they arrived on is unable to pick them up. They are forced to spend a night on the island with the bird, but it barely acknowledges them. It is determined that the creature is not a threat, and will be contained simply by baiting it away from coasts and sea lanes.

Hook: The Special Containment Procedure stands out compared to the SCPs I've read. The bird itself isn't dangerous enough to warrant destruction, and generally isolates itself. The Foundation would figure that it's more worthwhile to monitor it, and keep the thing away from humans.

This is my first Article, so I'm a bit nervous about it. Also, I'm aware that there is already a "Thunderbird" Article, but the concept for this one is completely different.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) Obligatory: New to this so expect some weird questions. So…is it possible to write a tale about an SCP without having an SCP article about said SCP? For some reason it felt like it was necessary to write the article about the SCP before the story about the SCP in order to get the number. The story is essentially written, I just wasn't sure if, for the purposes of this site, it was necessary to have the SCP first and then the story.

I'm just not sure about the order here. It just felt weird having the story first without having a number, if that makes any sense.

2) I was trying to keep it to the 400-word limit. This is a weird character to write about because The Foundation obviously wants to stop the character because the character's very existence requires the death of others, even as the character is on a road of self-discovery. The irony here is that the character is prevented from finding out the biggest part of who he is by the nature of his being.

[Yes, I was working on having the character basically working like a weekly show but from the bad guy's perspective, but where the bad guy didn't realize he was the bad guy.]

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlight] The Stone
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

SCP-XXXX can relay information from "Daddy"

how does it relay information and why would you call it daddy

Empirical evidence of -1's were discovered after findings of black slanted metamorphic spikes underneath the earth after excavation.

It's not actually clear what -1 is here; SCP-XXXX is the general rock, SCP-XXXX-2 is uh 'the father' but -1 is just kinda…there?

SCP-XXXX goes into a tantrum after being ignored for a prolonged amount of time. This results in a natural disaster 16 to 24 hours because of anger from -1 and -2.

I generally would urge you to avoid adding properties like this where it's like 'you have to interact with the SCP or bad things': having a reason for people to interact with it generally ends up with you creating a much more interesting narrative; whereas if they have to, it always makes the outcome of it feel…cheap

SCP-XXXX has a voice of a male baby

why?

His drunkenness also led him to come back to the facility one day and think that SCP-XXXX was the child he had with his women.

I do not like your new narrative and I think this line is perhaps the one I can best highlight to explain why: it's dumb, it feels irrelevant to the whole thing about like, the giant rock under the earth and the weather prediction and it doesn't really make any sense for a person to do.

I like the idea of using the Agent as a like, proxy for the father and having this kinda revolve around 'daddy' issues as a result but the actual execution feels extremely on the nose and just…ridiculous.

The juxtaposition of this rock being like…a baby and also calling for what is effectively the eradication of a country by natural disaster feels…jarring in an unpleasant way, in particular because the idea of this rock being a baby just feels…not good and also unclear as to why it's the case?

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

My biggest concerns with this SCP are twofold:

1. The entire proposal is extremely focussed on what the SCP is to the point where you don't even mention the PoV characters at all (i.e., the Foundation).

2. There's no real growth or change over it.

The first is my general sign that a tale from the perspective of the SCP might be more interesting than a SCP article, in that, if you think the SCPs internal life and what happens to them is the most interesting aspect of the story, it's generally best to tell the story from that perspective so you don't have to rely on the SCP telling the Foundation what's up. It's also generally a good idea if you don't have a strong thing for the Foundation to be trying to do because it means you don't have to worry about questions like 'why are the Foundation doing this'.

The second is a bigger concern: at the end of the day, you're trying to tell a story, and they're fundamentally characterised by things happening and like, characters changing or the situation they're in changing or w/e, and at the moment, it just feels…like you have a very generic overview of how this works without a clear like, end goal in mind? E.g., the SCP doesn't grow emotionally, they don't strive to overcome anything, there's not even any specific events mentioned; and I just really want to see something more concrete using this, y'know?

Forum thread: One More Week

item.title: Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

a feral humanoid fish with the traits of multiple types of marine life that has a fear of Doctors.

What kinda fish traits are we looking at here?

The SCP is one of multiple anomalous entities that were found by Foundation MTF agents that mentioned something about a hospital that hurt them, but after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents, the other entities and MTF agents were taken captive by an unknown threat. the SCP was found by another group of Foundation agents who found it unconscious and injured, along with a note from a Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks.

I'm a little uncertain as to how all this would be shown: like, the first part feels like it'd be vague communications and not really like, something fully in the article? And the second part feels…fine but like it has weird implications around this doctor that don't really go anywhere?

I think, at the end of the day, my biggest concern is that it feels too much like the focus of the narrative is on 'how did we find this thing' when to me the most interesting question is about what happens now it's contained: the fear of doctors and strange fishy nature feels like it'd give a lot of room for exploring how the foundation interacts with this, while the Dr Josef Monstrosity angle feels like it'd give a lot of room for exploring his role in this whole thing and like, what his existence means for the broader world.

It also feels like the narrative is very divorced from the actual scp: like my general rule of thumb is that if you could swap the scp object out for something with completely different properties, then the narrative is probably too broadly focussed.

item.title: SCP Proposal: The Red Girl (1st SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX, AKA the Red Girl, is a humanoid anomaly which takes the appearance of a 15-16 year old girl with with long hair and irises in a unnatural shade of bright red. The Red Girl shows usually sweet, affective behavior, but will get triggered if she gets visually or audibly exposed to rage or hatred, or senses rage in a nearby person. SCP-XXXX will undergo a rapid transformation, in which she grows red scales on 60% of her body, will grow claws and fangs and the hair will turn into spikes. SCP-XXXX will then attempt to viciously attack the person that it sensed the anger from, often resulting in a chain reaction if multiple people are nearby, although it will never attack more than 8 people in a row. After the attack, SCP-XXXX will show shock and remorse over its own deeds, and slowly regain her human appearance. Attempts learn SCP-XXXX to control this states have proven ineffective, as the Red Girl seems to lose all memories of the incident within the next 8 hours.

Central Narrative: Although the origins of the Red Girl are unknown, SCP-researchers have constructed several theories of why its attacks are aimed at people who carry negative feelings towards others: what if SCP-XXXX was created with the purpose of simply erasing all negative feelings in this world? Did the creator attempt to slowly rebuild a more positive and tolerant society? Or did they simply want to create a environment of fear and sadness for those who have committed the sin of wrath? The answer is still unknown, as SCP-XXXX doesn't seem to know herself about her creation and her memories of incidents continuously get erased.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the mystery of her creation might become an interesting topic. Furthermore, I think the Red Girl fits the category of humanoid SCP's who have limited power over their anomalous abilities and actions, such as SCP-053, SCP-073 or SCP-2662, without being too similar to either of them. I also feel an SCP with something that resembles a dual personality disorder is a rather unused concept.

item.title: The Hungry Constellation
item.content:encoded:
The anomaly is a constellation that can take the shape of any Earth-like creature that has a mouth that can be displayed easily in two-dimensions from a perspective, say, a beak. The anomaly is inactive by default, but can be activated for a while if a selected group of people see it, a group which I haven't decided on yet. Once activated, the jaws or beaks or etc. of the constellation closes very slowly, and anything that is 'inside' the jaw relative to the observer from the group of people is destroyed.

In a nutshell, a constellation that gets hungry when a select observer from a group of people sees it.

When I got to read "splashy time" I was already prepared to upvote, expecting a much needed light-hearted skip. However, all of this quickly went full 180 after I started reading the description. Using the designations and mentioning the recovery before actually saying what the objects are (in the 3rd paragraph no less) is a huge pet peeve of mine. This alone would warrant a downvote on any skip, no matter how brilliantly well-written it would otherwise be. Then there's the interview transcript, which I saw others enjoyed: it brings nothing new to the table (we already know the effects from the researcher-doctor text convo) and it makes sense that as soon as someone noticed the issue it be removed and rewritten properly.

I don't expect anyone to fix these issues since it's been so long since the article was written (which would normally rend this a necropost, for which I apologise), but if it happens I'll change my vote. Till then, however, it's a very firm downvote

item.title: The Lost Holiday Special
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: (Joke) SCP

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Weird

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP, extensive addenda describing discoveries.

Elevator Pitch: Finally, an answer to where all those Lost Christmas specials come from, where the end up, and why they're all so awful. This extensive research demonstrates both the anomalous nature of their appearance, and offers an occult explanation for their poor quality and untimely release.

Central Narrative: Although the '78 Star Wars special is probably the best known, some paranormal entity has been producing anomalous media since at least 1976. The addenda include selected summaries such as "The 007 Days of Christmas" (1976), "A Very Rocky Christmas" (1979), "The Blues Brothers: A Mission From God" (1998), and "The Festivus Reunion" (2015), all featuring appropriately aged (or decayed) actors reprising their original roles.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Let's be honest. The universe would be a better place if we could blame every holiday special on some unknowable force.

item.title: The Sandman (GREENLIGHT WANTED)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: A horrific humanoid that makes any person they encounter a narcoleptic, anyone affected by the humanoid will be stalked until they fall asleep which they will then enter the Sandman’s dreamscape where they are lured into a sense of security before being murdered and/or eaten alive gruesomely through mutilation. The subject of this encounter will be conscious the whole time while they’re unable to escape as it slowly eats and/or mutilates the subject. The victim is driven to insanity before the end of this encounter. When the victim awakens due to his unhinged state, they are a severe danger to everything around them.

Central Narrative: A husband comes home to find his wife and kids mutilated corpses on the floor. As he begins to cry, he falls to the floor to awaken in a dream state where he sees his wife sitting on a shorefront. He approaches her but as he gets close her head spins around revealing a disgusting face with a split jaw. Her limbs and skin start to turn into sand and fall off revealing something that so ugly and hideous he starts to puke. He can’t stop eventually starts to puke out blood trying to scream for help. It slowly approaches him and as it does the man stops puking only for his jaw to be ripped off and his frontal lobe to be crushed by the creature’s mouth where he is then eaten alive, completely conscious throughout the whole experience. He wakes up next to his dead family and he is extremely over joyous. He starts kicking over furniture and jumping on his deceased family’s corpses while cackling. He stomps his infant’s corpse to a pulp and exclaims, “This is the best day of m,” before he is cut off as his jaw shoots off, a big portion of his frontal lobe vanishing instantly, his ribcage snapping open to reveal nothing inside. Before he even hits, he is already dead. The creature is satisfied as he looks down on the dead family, it looks out the window to see more flesh to be devoured and the cycle starts again.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Entity based on the Ole Lukøje that connects a subject’s experience in their dream world to reality. "It dragged me into my nightmare where it wished for all to feed its slumbering insanity."

Additional Notes: Feedback on the hook if anything.

Additionally, rather than writing vehement posts like this which will disappear if the page is slated for standard deletion, you can state complaints here: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-5797485/complaints-thread or contact a staff member about the situation.

Also, as an aside, one's forum posts can be read via the "recent posts and comments" section of a wikidot profile. Misrepresentation of reviewer interactions doesn't really encourage reviewers to want to assist an author.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-5136

Hoo boy…

Here's a crit.
On a pale horse...

SCP-5129 is to be kept in a 15m x 15m Titanium room

Aaand that's a downvote. Titanium shouldn't be capitalized. Horses generally need two acres of land- about 8km2 of land. 15mx15m is about 225m, far too small. Finally, titanium is only useful if you need something both light and strong. Otherwise, reinforced steel is almost always going to be better.

Steel shackles are to be locked to SCP-5129 hind legs to at least slow it down.

… how? I mean, how is this supposed to slow it down? Also; bad tone. "The rear legs of SCP-5129 are to be shackled to inhibit its maximum speed" is better.

Reinforced sliding steel doors are locked in place when SCP-5129 goes on its rampage.

… See, now this would be an appropriate use of titanium or (more likely) a steel/titanium alloy. Regardless, unless material requirements are of the "substitutes WILL cause a breach" nature, you're likeoy better off not mentioning them.

Also, "rampaging" or rage states aren't really seen as interesting. They're boting, and generally never used now.

Two foundation agents who have taken courses on exorcism and have been dispatched by their teacher are to be kept at SCP-5129's containment cell at all times.

… what kind of exorcism? Shinto exorcisms are much different than catholic exorcisms. Furthermore, based on the SCP, it's unclear how an exorcist or someone with exorcist training would help here, as the idea of an exorcist is to banish evil spirits/demons from a host, object, or place.

As for the SCP itself, you've basically failed to understand ancient greek mythology. They have three seperate sections of Hades, the underworld. First, the greeks had Elisyum, a paradise where the truly blessed and honored would go upon death. Then you have Tartarus, their equivalent of hell where the Titans and those who commited truly reprehensible acts would go for eternal torment. Finally, you had Asphereus, where everyone else went; neither reward nor punishment, the souls of people sent here would be wandering aimlessly, forever caught up in the moment of their demise unless stirred out of it by mortals visiting the place.

None of these places are said to resemble what you described in the exploration.

Furthermore, a creature like this would most likely be associated with Ares, the God of War, not Hades, the God of Death, considering its habit to raid and pillage its local environs.

I strongly recommend you go to the site forums and work on the core concept of this, rather than go to the draft stage. The flaws of this SCP are fundamental in nature, beyond what I've mentioned, and attempting to draft it without focusing on the core concepts first will make it harder to fix.

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there undeadmuffin. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

So on the surface this seems like an overly-simple concept: you have a basic compulsion effect (the pen forces the writer to think/write whatever it’s thinking). You also have a simple page outline where you’ve listed some examples of what the pen will be writing (I’m assuming these will come across on the page as journal entries detailing the pen’s prior life).

I’m left wondering if that’s all to the concept… Because if so, it’s not a very compelling article on its own. You yourself have mentioned that it’s “ink pen meets Forrest Gump,”, so what’s so different about the story compared to that of the film? If you’re comparing it to a film, is there going to be a beginning, middle and end? Even, an article solely comprised of the pen’s backstory isn’t very compelling.

Basically, I’m pushing you to give us more. The concept on its own is workable, but the events you’ve described surrounding the anomaly isn’t very exciting at the moment.

Basically the fleeting and uncertainty of life as told by an ink pen that has gathered a number of life experiences over the decades.

This is an example of an idea / theme, but your article should not revolve around it by itself. Rather, it should come out through the story that you tell. Some more questions you can consider:

1. Who made the pen? Why did it trap itself within a pen in the first place? What goals did the entity have before it was trapped? What does it want now besides being mopey?

2. How does the Foundation contain it? There should be some difficulty here or consequence of containment failure. Does its existential thoughts influence the researchers it comes into contact with, for example? If it’s Thaumiel, how then will the scp be used by the Foundation?

3. What are you trying to say by the end of the article. Right now, the message is simply: life sucks. Is that really all you want the readers to feel?

If you decide to revise the concept further / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply. Best of luck!

I think you mean viscous, he's not spilling out Roman settlements when he bleeds, unless he is, that would be very, very interesting.

I see you are looking to create a narrative around this, and I highly encourage you to do so but don't rely on critters to think one up for you. Good luck author.

item.title: They Just Keep Searching
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I posted this one before, but that was well over two weeks ago and it didn't get any responses. Figured I might as well try this forum again before looking into other critique options :) (I have made some very slight modifications since, anyway).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make heavy use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 10 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Eventually these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and high resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Will search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP idea so I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away! I'm still trying to think of a better name for it.
